dedupe_keys.name: trabzon turkey gps based route optimisation of solid waste collection and hauling for 39 districts

description: This case study optimises the routes of solid waste collection and hauling in Trabzon, a city of about 185,000 inhabitants in north-eastern Turkey. It was published in the Global NEST Journal. The authors note that collection and hauling make up about 85 percent of total disposal spending, so reducing empty travel saves money. They filmed the collection process with a video camera and collected data on current spending, truck types and capacities, waste production, population and GPS traces of every route, then applied a shortest path model to 39 districts of the city with the aim of minimum cost, using the Route View Pro software as the optimisation tool. The article is available online as a free PDF on the journal website. Coverage is the city's collection system at the time of the study. Caveats: the paper's author list and results are not given in the metadata used here and must be read in the article; savings depend on the routes and fleet at the time. Simulation uses: GPS-based collection route data and a documented procedure for calibrating collection and hauling cost models in mid-sized cities. Related records: the Onitsha route optimisation (case_study-onitsha-solid-waste-collection-route-optimisation) applies a routing heuristic in Nigeria, and the Saltillo instances (data-saltillo-waste-collection-2ecvrp-if-instances) give routing benchmarks.
